Who I Am

About Me

Teaching was not my first career choice — I was initially drawn to the medical field. However, over time I developed a genuine passion for education, especially in working with children. This led me to pursue a degree in Special Needs Education, which has deepened my understanding of inclusive and learner-centered teaching.

"Every learner is unique and capable of growth when given the right support and opportunities. Education should be inclusive, compassionate, and responsive to the needs of all students."

As a future educator, I aim to create a learning environment where no student is left behind and where each learner is encouraged to reach their full potential. I integrate digital tools into my practice to support engaging and effective learning experiences.

Growth Mindset

Reflection Logs

Where I Used IT
I used tools such as Canva and Google Docs to prepare lesson plans and instructional materials for my demo teaching and class presentations. I also used spreadsheets to organize data efficiently, which saved time and will be useful for recording students' grades in the future.
Where Will I Use IT
As a future Special Needs Education teacher, I will use these tools to create simple, engaging, and adapted learning materials that support diverse learners. I may also use platforms like Google Classroom for communication, sharing resources, and conducting meetings when needed.
How IT Shaped Me as a Student
Digital tools transformed how I study and prepare. They helped me become more organized, creative in lesson design, and effective in communicating educational content — skills I will carry into my teaching career.
Am I Ready for the IT Era?
Yes. I believe that teaching in the IT Era requires continuous learning, adaptability, and a willingness to grow. As a future Special Needs Education teacher, I am motivated to keep improving my skills and to stay updated with new technologies that can support inclusive learning.

I am committed to using digital tools not only to make lessons more engaging, but also to ensure that every learner, regardless of their needs, has the opportunity to understand and succeed. With this mindset, I am ready to face the challenges of a technology-integrated classroom and to become a teacher who makes a meaningful difference in students' lives.
